newsitem.title: USA: Duke Oconee, S.C. nuke units to shut down.
newsitem.headline: Duke Oconee, S.C. nuke units to shut down.

text.p: Two of Duke Power Co's 846 megawatt Oconee nuclear power units in South Carolina were expected to shut down over the next several days, according to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC).
Oconee unit 1 had reduced power to 15 percent of capacity as of early Friday and would go to cold shutdown in about three days, the NRC said in its daily plant status report.
The Seneca, S.C. unit was "holding power for piping inspections, will go to cold shutdown in approximately three days," the NRC said.
Also, the Oconee unit 3 "will begin unit shutdown later today," the NRC said Friday.
Oconee 3, also located at Seneca with a capacity of 846 megawatts, was operating at 100 percent of capacity as of early Friday morning.
No explanation was given for the Oconee 3 shutdown. The unit was scheduled to go into a 50-day refueling and maintenance outage beginning November 3.
Company officials were not immediately available for comment on the Oconee shutdowns.
Oconee unit 2 has been shutdown since Sept 24 following a heater drain pipe rupture which injured seven plant workers.
No schedule has been set for a restart of Oconee 2, and company officials have said there was no rush to resume operations while the cause of the pipeline rupture was being investigated.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
